strengths: The mean-point correspondence is a simple and useful contribution: it enables four-point three-view hypothesis generation using established five-point and P3P solvers. Avoiding specialized polynomial machinery or learned initialization makes the approach attractive for practical geometric vision.

The empirical support is extensive: 90,000 triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, evaluation within both PoseLib and GC-RANSAC, and supplementary tests covering noise, geometry, outliers, thresholds, and individual scenes. Table 6 also confirms improvements under a stricter metric incorporating all three camera pairs.

The results demonstrate useful operating points against an enhanced baseline. On PhotoTourism, 4p3v(M)+R+F+ENM achieves AUC@10 of 76.16 at 44.51 ms, versus 76.20 at 56.52 ms for 5pt+P3P+R+F+ENM. This supports practical value even without uniformly superior accuracy.

The ablations clarify the importance of refinement, filtering, and early non-minimal refitting. Hyperparameters are selected on a held-out scene, and the manuscript provides code and archived data links. These supported practical contributions make the overall case favor acceptance.
weaknesses: The runtime comparison with homotopy continuation is confounded by initialization. Section 8.3 reports approximately 45 ms of network/data loading once per RANSAC invocation, a substantial cost relative to HC's reported 60–67 ms total runtimes in Table 2. Without separating initialization from repeated estimation, the claimed speed advantage is not established for applications that retain the loaded model.

The strongest speed–accuracy claims exceed the comparison provided against the enhanced five-point baseline. Figure 4 omits its +R+F variants, although Table 2 shows these modifications improve it substantially. The fully enhanced shifted solver gains only 0.94 AUC@10 points on PhotoTourism over the fully enhanced baseline while taking 112.60 versus 56.52 ms. Its advantage at equal runtime therefore remains unresolved.

The theoretical guarantee is limited to the virtual correspondence's point-to-epipolar-line distance, bounded by the image triangle's size. It does not establish a useful pose-error bound or convergence to the correct refinement basin. Figure 9 shows residual errors even on noiseless inputs. The method is convincingly evaluated as an approximate hypothesis generator, but the stronger claim that ENM makes scene dependence negligible lacks comparable analytical support.

Some implementation details remain insufficiently specified for independent reproduction. Section 3.1 jumps from estimating the affine fundamental matrix to triangulation without explaining its conversion into calibrated camera poses. The three-view LM refinement also lacks an explicit residual definition and pose/scale parameterization. These are correctable documentation gaps, but matter for a paper emphasizing easy reimplementation.
